summary: Earlier rows isolate rules on controlled edited copies of real English sentences, with similarity fixed at 1. C-16 adds whole-family-held-out, audit-authored cross-language equivalents and mutations of source-backed facts, reporting measured paired similarities separately from rule-only stress. All labels are construction labels, not human labels; paired tests exclude retrieval.
limitations: No human labels, calibrated model judges, whole-article LLM baseline, or real-world contradiction accuracy. The initial held-out scores were seen before v2; only the fresh held-out articles were reserved before that change. Name swaps remain outside the rules and are counted as misses. Model/API cost for these local rules is zero; hardware and hosting costs are not estimated. C-16 frozen whole-family audit: measured cross-language pairs caught 5/36 planted errors and falsely flagged 2/57 constructed equivalents. These are audit-authored translations, not human labels. Combined metadata rename/reverse insertion changed 25/742 top-three rankings. The original natural retrieval test favored lexical, 8/9 vs vector 7/9; C-16 held-out proxy also favored lexical, 4/4 vs vector 3/4. Disagreement introduction at revision X remains unproven. Live SQL still requires this Mac and its temporary tunnel. See the ledger for sealed traces.
